blocks.text: Mystical visions: strange sightings at Bristol photo festival – in pictures
From women floating across the shore to magical patches of Irish land, this year’s exhibitions are full of fantastic yet confounding photography
Thu 5 Nov 2026 02.00 EST

blocks.alt: The artist’s parents lie on a large rubbish pile, one in an orange gown, one in green suit, gazing skyward

blocks.text: Liu Hsing Yu, My father & mother

Family Times is at Centrespace Gallery, Bristol, until 11 November. In collaboration with Ministry of Culture, Republic of China (Taiwan). All shows are a part of Bristol photo festival Photograph: Liu Hsing Yu

blocks.alt: Annie Wang stands by a camera tripod beside a boy, with a framed family photo behind

blocks.text: Annie Wang, The Mother as a Creator

blocks.alt: A double-exposed image shows soldiers crouching and advancing through smoke, from The Magic Labyrinth

blocks.text: Julián Barón, The Magic Labyrinth
No Pasarán by Anna Jornet, Julián Barón and Natasha Christia
is at Redcliffe Caves, Bristol, until 15 November. In collaboration with Institut Ramon Llull,
Acción Cultural Española and Insitituto Cervantes Photograph: Julián Barón

blocks.alt: George Hallett, Mongezi Feza (Musician) & friend at home. London, 1973

blocks.text: George Hallett, Mongezi Feza (musician) and friend at home, London, 1973
George Hallett: Home and Exile is at IC Visual Lab, Bristol until 15 November. In collaboration with Liverpool John Moores University Photograph: Courtesy George Hallett Research Collection

blocks.alt: A dusty alarm clock, kettle and old telephone sit on a stone ledge in a Welsh mine

blocks.text: Kjell-Åke Andersson, Bargoed Colliery, Wales, 1973-76

Dark Tales: British Documentary Photography and the Gothic is at Martin Parr Foundation, Bristol, until 20 December. In collaboration with Martin Parr Foundation. See more in our gallery Photograph: Kjell-Åke Andersson

blocks.alt: A split, mirrored image shows a figure in a white dress with arms outstretched, doubled above and below a log

blocks.text: Maria Lax, from the series Stray Sod
Stray Sod by Maria Lax at the Welcome Building, Bristol, until 15 November. In collaboration with Frame | Contemporary, Art Finland Photograph: Maria Lax

blocks.alt: A grimy red darkroom sink or floor with mineral stains surrounds a dark drain

blocks.text: Michel Campeau, from the series Darkroom
Darkroom by Michel Campeau is at Arnos Vale Cemetery, Bristol, until 20 December. In collaboration with Martin Parr Foundation Photograph: Michel Campeau

blocks.alt: A couple walks arm in arm along a beach, with palm trees beyond and the photographer’s shadow visible

blocks.text: Photos by Kegham Djeghalian Sr

Photo Kegham by Kegham Djeghalian Jr is at Albion Dockside, Bristol, until 15 December. In collaboration with Photopia (Cairo, Egypt), supported by the British Council Photograph: Courtesy of Kegham Djeghalian Jr.

blocks.alt: Joy Gregory, in a leopard-print jacket, adjusts an orange wig at an outdoor market stall

blocks.text: Joy Gregory, Stockwell Siren from the series Celebrity Blonde, 2003 performance
Joy Gregory: Catching Flies With Honey is at Arnolfini, Bristol, until 7 February 2027. Exhibition originated by Whitechapel Gallery Photograph: Joy Gregory

blocks.alt: Rows of old wooden chairs face a small lectern in Bristol Cathedral’s empty room

blocks.text: Holly Lynton, from the series Beyond the Bounds
Beyond the Bounds by Holly Lynton is at Bristol Cathedral until 11 November. In collaboration with Bristol Cathedral, Spectrum and HAPAX Photograph: Holly Lynton

blocks.alt: Collage of flying crows, a clay sculpture, and riverside village life in Bangladesh

blocks.text: Akshay Mahajan, People of Clay
People of Clay by Akshay Mahajan is at Bristol Museum and Art Gallery until 14 February. In collaboration with Bristol Museum & Art Galleries, Friends of BMAG and ArtFund Photograph: Akshay Mahajan

blocks.alt: Children play on a sandy riverbank beneath a large cut-out photographic image of a woman floating in the sky, from People of Clay

blocks.text: Akshay Mahajan, People of Clay, 2022

blocks.alt: An orange marker sketch of a tall chair-like structure overlays a close-up photo of a bird’s beak

blocks.text: Sheida Soleimani, from the series Persistence Studies
Persistence Studies is at Bristol Museum & Art Gallery until 14 February 2027. In collaboration with Brigstow Institute and Bristol Museum and Art Galleries Photograph: Sheida Solemani.

blocks.alt: Two men, Rashid Mahdi on the left

blocks.text: Untitled (Rashid Mahdi, left), c. 1955

One of Many: An Alternative History of Photography is at Albion Dockside, Bristol, until 15 November. In collaboration with the French Institute in the UK Photograph: Claude Germain/Musée du quai Branly–Jacques Chirac, Paris
